description: LUKS (Leistungsuntersuchung Knoten und Strecken, capacity analysis of nodes and lines) is a commercial software suite for railway operations studies, developed by VIA Consulting & Development, now part of quattron. Its base module holds editors for master data, railway infrastructure and train data with standard interfaces for infrastructure and timetable imports, and computes microscopic running and blocking times for every train run, following DB InfraGO practice and UIC Code 406. Modules add graphic timetable construction with conflict detection (LUKS-K), analytical bottleneck assessment based on queueing theory (LUKS-A), event-driven simulation of operations with random disturbances, dispatching and rescheduling to measure robustness and capacity (LUKS-S), global timetable optimisation that resolves conflicts and maximises buffers (LUKS-OptDis), capacity evaluation after UIC 406 (LUKS-C), and usage indicators for infrastructure elements such as switches to guide maintenance (LUKS-ISN). Coverage: any railway network the user models, mainly used in German-speaking countries. Access: licensed from quattron; the product page is in German. Licence and cost: proprietary and paid. Caveats: no public documentation of algorithms or validation, and data preparation is heavy. It supports rail capacity planning, delay propagation analysis and timetable optimisation. It is a commercial counterpart to the open-source OSRD platform and to the OpenTrack simulation used in the ProRail timetable case study, both in the catalogue.
